project_scope.note: Built around axillary tendrils and the corona/androgynophore flower.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: At several leafy nodes of local Passiflora, locate a single tendril originating in the leaf axil, then examine the open flower: a corona of filaments surrounds an elevated androgynophore carrying five stamens and a superior ovary, commonly with three styles. Fruit with multiple arillate seeds is a further confirmation. Leaf lobing and flower size vary; a detached coiled tendril does not prove its insertion.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Alternate, often lobed, with stipules; petiolar glands may occur.
family_diagnostics.flower: 5 sepals + 5 petals around a conspicuous corona; stamens and ovary elevated on an androgynophore/gynophore.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Berry-like or capsular with arillate seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Passiflora: leaf-axillary tendril + corona + elevated reproductive column. Compare node insertion against grape (leaf-opposed), greenbrier (paired petiole-base tendrils) and cucurbits (lateral tendril); confirm flower anatomy when attachment is unclear.
look_here_first_sequence: Inspect a complete node for a leaf-axillary tendril; a coiled tendril without its attachment is not sufficient proof.
Inspect the open flower for corona filaments and an elevated androgynophore bearing stamens and the superior ovary.
Confirm a fruit with multiple seeds and fleshy arils; distinguish from dry Convolvulaceae capsules.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Passionflowers practically label themselves once you know where to look: axillary tendril, corona, and the elevated reproductive column.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the flower
steps.look_for: A conspicuous corona surrounding the elevated stamens and ovary.
steps.why_it_matters: The flower architecture is one of the most distinctive local family signatures.

steps.title: 2 · See flower and fruit together
steps.look_for: Flower architecture and developing berry-like fruit on the same vine.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects flower morphology to reproductive outcome.

steps.title: 3 · Read the leaf and node
steps.look_for: Alternate leaf plus tendril arising from the axil.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates passionflower vines from grape vines before flowering.

steps.title: 4 · Count the styles
steps.look_for: Three prominent styles/stigmas above the stamens.

comparisons.title: Passifloraceae vs Vitaceae
comparisons.rule: Passiflora tendrils are axillary and flowers are showy with corona + reproductive column; Vitis tendrils/inflorescences are commonly opposite the leaf and flowers are tiny.

comparisons.title: Passifloraceae vs Convolvulaceae
comparisons.rule: Morning-glories twine with the stem and have a plicate fused corolla; Passiflora uses axillary tendrils and a corona/androgynophore.

comparisons.title: Passifloraceae vs Cucurbitaceae
comparisons.rule: Passiflora flower has a superior ovary on an elevated column; typical female cucurbit flower has an inferior ovary. Tendrils alone overlap.

comparisons.title: Passifloraceae vs Smilacaceae
comparisons.rule: Smilax typically has a pair of tendrils from the petiole-base region and small unisexual flowers with six tepals; local Passiflora usually has one axillary tendril and a corona with elevated stamens/ovary. Confirm on an intact node, not a detached tendril.

visual_lesson.caveat: This is a Passiflora-centered local module, not a claim that all Passifloraceae are tendrilled vines. Passiflora foetida's finely divided sticky bracts and P. tenuiloba's highly variable leaf outlines are species-level traits, not universal family characters. A flower-front photograph alone may not establish the ovary's superior position or the base of the androgynophore.
diagnostic_photo_needs: Intact Passiflora node showing axillary tendril origin and stipules
Side-on open flower showing corona, androgynophore, five stamens, three styles and superior ovary
Matched grape leaf-opposed tendril and cucurbit tendril insertion at comparable scale
Fruit section showing fleshy arils around seeds
Matched same-scale intact-node macros: Passiflora axillary tendril, Vitaceae leaf-opposed tendril, Smilax paired petiole-base tendrils and Cucurbitaceae lateral tendril.
Opened fruit with individually resolved seeds and fleshy arils; label seed, aril and fruit wall only after visual inspection.

genus_routing.scope: Project pool is Passiflora-centered; these are species-level cues, not universal family characters.

routes.cue: small greenish flowers, usually shallow three-lobed leaves and small dark berries; inspect node and flower
finely divided bracts envelop flower/fruit; corona visible in flower; do not assume all passionflowers have a bract cage
large maypop flower and relatively large fleshy fruit; confirm with flower architecture
leaf blades may be narrow or variably lobed on one species; confirm with flower and node
